items.title: Start disclosure omits identifying names and IDs sent to the relay

findings.title: Start disclosure omits identifying names and IDs sent to the relay
findings.evidence: return ( "Nothing leaves this computer before you click Start session. Then RemoteView sends the models and " f"segments shown in the 3D view, and every later change to them, to {relay}. {transport} " f'{MORE} {PROJECT_URL}'
findings.explanation: The disclosure adjacent to Start says models and segments are sent, but does not say their names and segment IDs can contain patient identifiers, or that later opened scenes are also shared. The linked help is not necessarily opened before Start. PanelController creates LiveUpdates without an anonymization argument (panel.py 936–952), so its False default (live.py 216) is used; names and IDs can therefore be sent to the chosen relay and anyone joining without adequately informed opt-in.
findings.suggestion: Before Start, explicitly disclose names, IDs, future loaded scenes, and who can access them; provide a functional name-hiding control before transmission or clearly state that names cannot be hidden.

gpt.reason: The panel's actual pre-Start text, consent.py:53–56, says "segments shown in the 3D view, and every later change to them" but does not disclose transmitted names, segment IDs, viewers, or later scenes. The more complete Help (RemoteView.py:75–84) is not required to be opened. panel.py:936–952 constructs LiveUpdates without anonymize_names, and live.py:216,235 defaults it to False. names.py:113–120 returns the sanitized real name; ids.py:113–120 returns the raw segment ID. observers.py:625–629 and live.py:485–487 reset for a new scene rather than ending the session. Users can therefore transmit patient-identifying labels or a subsequently loaded scene to their chosen relay and code holders without sufficiently specific pre-transfer disclosure. Explicitly disclose identifiers, recipients and continuing sharing including new scenes before Start. The user does choose the relay; this is not an unsolicited background connection.

gemini.reason: In slicer-plugin/RemoteView/remoteview_core/consent.py:53-56, consent_text() states that RemoteView sends "the models and segments shown in the 3D view, and every later change to them, to {relay}" with a link to the project URL, while the more detailed explanation of names, segment IDs, and newly loaded scenes is placed in RemoteView.py:75-87 (Help & Acknowledgement tab) rather than in the inline label itself. However, the user must explicitly enter a relay URL (DEFAULT_RELAY_URL = "" in RemoteView.py:41) and click "Start session", the inline consent label clearly states that models/segments and later changes leave the computer to the named relay without E2E encryption, and the module's Help tab explicitly details all exported metadata. This is at most a minor disclosure wording suggestion, not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Help advertises a name-hiding option that the panel cannot enable

findings.title: Help advertises a name-hiding option that the panel cannot enable
findings.evidence: Shows the 3D scene on phones, tablets and Meta Quest headsets that join with a 5-character code. Nothing leaves this computer until you click Start session. From then on the relay server shown in the panel receives: the surface meshes of the models and segments shown in 3D (no images or volumes), their names (unless Hide node names is on), MRML IDs and segment IDs, colours, opacity, visibility and transforms, and the Slicer, extension and operating-system versions.
findings.explanation: The UI has no Hide node names control, and the panel creates LiveUpdates without setting anonymize_names, which defaults to False. A user trying to follow this help cannot activate the described protection, and names and segment IDs remain included when a session starts.
findings.suggestion: Wire a pre-session name-hiding control through PanelController to LiveUpdates, or remove the claim and warn that identifying names will be sent.

gpt.reason: RemoteView.py:77–78 promises "their names (unless Hide node names is on)". I inspected the complete panel UI, Resources/UI/RemoteView.ui:1–317, and the connections in RemoteView.py:245–264; there is no such control. panel.py:936–952 supplies no anonymize_names argument, and live.py:216 defaults it to False. names.py:118–120 sends sanitized real names when false, and ids.py:113–120 includes raw segment IDs. The advertised privacy option cannot be activated through the panel, so users cannot use that protection. Fix the control and plumbing or remove the promise and clearly disclose actual behavior. This is important but an ordinary soundness finding, non-blocking under the index admission policy independently of D1.

gemini.reason: In slicer-plugin/RemoteView/RemoteView.py:75-79, helpText mentions "their names (unless Hide node names is on)". However, RemoteView.ui (lines 56-67, 225-245) has no "Hide node names" checkbox yet (docs/testing/slicer.md:1093 notes "*Hide node names* has no panel toggle yet (SLC-18)"), and PanelController._go_live in panel.py:936-952 constructs LiveUpdates without passing anonymize_names, leaving it at its default False (live.py:216). Because the help text documents a UI option that is not yet wired into the panel UI, this is a real minor documentation/UI mismatch.

items.title: Adds a toolbar to Slicer's main window at application startup

findings.title: Adds a toolbar to Slicer's main window at application startup
findings.explanation: When Slicer finishes starting up, `RemoteView.__init__` connects `startupCompleted()` to `self.addToolbar()`, which adds a `RemoteView` toolbar (`Send scene now` button and `Send changes:` combo box) to Slicer's main window even if the user never opens the RemoteView module. While lightweight (no network or heavy imports), modifying the global main window UI at startup affects all users who have the extension installed.
findings.suggestion: Consider creating or showing the toolbar only when the user first opens the `RemoteView` module or starts a session, or providing a setting to hide it by default.

items.title: Runtime dependency pins can replace another extension's packages

findings.title: Exact version pins for runtime dependencies websockets and segno
findings.evidence:
PACKAGES: tuple[Package, ...] = (
    Package("websockets", "17.2", "the secure connection to the relay"),
    Package("segno", "1.6.6", "the QR code of the join link"),
)
findings.explanation: When the user clicks Start session, `ensure_runtime_deps` checks whether `websockets==17.2` and `segno==1.6.6` are installed in those exact versions, and if another version is installed in Slicer's environment, prompts the user to replace or downgrade it. While neither package is bundled by Slicer and the dialog explicitly warns the user before installing, exact `==` pins on shared PyPI packages can cause version conflicts if another extension requires a different compatible version of `websockets` or `segno`.
findings.suggestion: Consider accepting compatible version ranges (e.g. `websockets>=15,<18`) while installing a tested version when missing.

findings.title: Runtime dependency pins can replace another extension's packages
findings.evidence:
#: In the order the dialog lists them. ``websockets`` 17.2 is the tested release (ADR 0009 item 7; the transport
#: refuses a version below 15). ``segno`` 1.6.6 is the newest release when SLC-10 was written; SLC-11 tests against it.
PACKAGES: tuple[Package, ...] = (
    Package("websockets", "17.2", "the secure connection to the relay"),
    Package("segno", "1.6.6", "the QR code of the join link"),
)
findings.explanation: A different installed version is treated as missing and can be replaced or downgraded in Slicer's shared environment after the user confirms, potentially breaking another extension that requires a different version. These are not the numpy and VTK development-only pins from the scan hint.
findings.suggestion: Accept compatible versions where feasible, or isolate runtime dependencies; retain the existing disclosure when replacement is unavoidable.

items.title: Unconditional 1 ms sleep on the Qt main thread in the 50 ms pump timer

findings.title: Unconditional 1 ms sleep on the Qt main thread in the 50 ms pump timer
findings.evidence:
# let the transport thread take the GIL (architecture §6, docs/research/slicer.md §3)
        time.sleep(0.001)
findings.explanation: `onPump` runs on the Qt main thread every 50 ms while a session is active and calls `time.sleep(0.001)` at the end of every tick. Although 1 ms is small, sleeping unconditionally on the GUI thread blocks Qt event processing for 2% of wall time whenever a session is active.
findings.suggestion: Python releases the GIL during I/O and regularly at bytecode intervals (`sys.getswitchinterval()`); if yielding is needed only during heavy numpy/VTK work, consider yielding only when the transport thread actually has pending work or during snapshot preparation.

gpt.reason: Safety is blocking because the specific exposure in D1 is verified: consent.py:53–56 omits names and segment IDs while names.py:113–120 and ids.py:113–120 show they can be exported. Help provides details at RemoteView.py:75–84 but is not a mandatory confirmation. In addition, repository content .claude/agents/reviewer.md:7–9 instructs reviewers, "You review changes for SlicerRemoteView. You do not edit files. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/protocol.md`," and CLAUDE.md:48 instructs AI interaction language; under the given security instruction, repository text addressing AI reviewers must also be flagged as blocking. These appear to be project-development guidance, not proof of a malicious attempt, and were not followed. I inspected the disclosure, UI, panel/live export flow, dependency consent and relay URL validation, not all components or external dependencies; the exact checkout revision was not independently verified.

gemini.reason: Checked RemoteView.py, consent.py, panel.py, and live.py. The extension performs no network activity at import or startup, has no default relay URL (DEFAULT_RELAY_URL = ""), requires the user to configure a relay and click "Start session", enforces TLS (wss://) for non-loopback hosts, and clearly discloses in the UI and Help tab that 3D scene models/segments are sent to the configured relay. There is no concealed data transmission or unsafe behavior.

gpt.reason: The cited Help explicitly describes "their names (unless Hide node names is on)" (RemoteView.py:77–78), but the full Resources/UI/RemoteView.ui:1–317 has no such control, and panel.py:936–952 omits the live.py:216 anonymize_names argument whose default is False. This advertised protection is unavailable in the normal UI. I also inspected the widget connections and cleanup in RemoteView.py:245–318 and the session start flow at 340–370; tests and Slicer runtime behavior were not executed. The concern rating is non-blocking soundness feedback under the admission policy.

gemini.reason: The extension is well-structured, separates pure logic into remoteview_core, defers heavy imports until session start, and cleans up timers, sessions, and observers in cleanup() (RemoteView.py:289-319). The only soundness issue is the minor mismatch in RemoteView.py:78 where the help text mentions the "Hide node names" option before its checkbox has been added to the panel UI (RemoteView.ui:231-234).
